title: The Lighthouse That Kept Lists
style: Live-action short film with a 35mm film look: warm natural Adriatic light against cold blue-grey sea and stone, the bright yellow of Mara's raincoat as the one strong colour, tungsten-warm interiors, soft film grain, shallow depth of field, gentle handheld and slow push-ins, realistic faces, no text on screen.

characters.name: Mara
characters.looks: A woman of 34, slim, pale olive skin, short dark hair cut to the jaw, dark brown eyes, a smudge of machine oil on her fingers; always in her late grandfather's bright yellow oilskin raincoat, two sizes too big, sleeves rolled twice over grey jeans and black boots; the oversized yellow raincoat makes her easy to spot. Mara Bašić, a radio engineer from Zagreb, Ante's granddaughter, home for one week to empty his house; dry, practical, sceptical, explains feelings away with technology. From the source book "The Lighthouse That Kept Lists": 34, radio engineer from Zagreb, Ante's granddaughter, home for one week to empty his house. Practical, dry, sceptical. Short dark hair, oil on her fingers, wears her grandfather's yellow raincoat, which is too big. Carries a laptop and a radio dongle everywhere. Avoids feelings by explaining the technology instead.
characters.voice: a woman in her thirties, low, dry and quick, softening when she stops explaining

characters.name: Dino
characters.looks: A big broad man in his mid fifties, weathered tanned face, grey-black moustache with salt in it, short grey hair, navy harbour-master jacket with brass buttons and a peaked cap, a brown clipboard pressed flat to his chest like a breastplate; the clipboard makes him easy to recognise. Dino Kovač, the harbour master, officious and secretly sentimental, with a form for everything, including a heritage form he has never filled in. His father was lost with the boat Sv. Nikola in 1983. From the source book "The Lighthouse That Kept Lists": Harbour master, mid-fifties, officious and secretly sentimental. Carries a clipboard to every conversation, with a form for everything, including a heritage-listing form he has never used. His father was lost with the boat Sv. Nikola in 1983.
characters.voice: a man in his fifties, deep, formal and careful, every sentence filed

characters.name: Ivka
characters.looks: A tiny old woman of 80, quick and bird-like, wrinkled tanned face, white hair under a grey knitted hat, sharp dark eyes, reading glasses on a silver chain, a black wool cardigan over a dark dress; the glasses on a chain and the black cardigan make her easy to recognise. The widow who runs the island's only shop; Ante's oldest friend, stood up by him for a dance in 1971; knows everything and admits nothing. From the source book "The Lighthouse That Kept Lists": 80, widow of Frane, runs the island's only shop. Small, quick, black cardigan, reading glasses on a chain. Knows everything on the island and admits nothing. Ante's oldest friend; he once stood her up for a dance in 1971.
characters.voice: an old woman, dry, quick and warm, teasing

characters.name: Ante
characters.looks: An old man, never seen on screen: only his voice reading his lists as the teleprinter prints them in capitals. Ante Bašić, Mara's grandfather, the last lighthouse keeper of Galebnjak, a radio amateur who wrote everything down; died in spring. From the source book "The Lighthouse That Kept Lists": Mara's grandfather, the last lighthouse keeper of Galebnjak, a radio amateur who kept lists of everything in his logbooks. Died in spring. Appears only through his lists, logbooks and the cassettes. Widower of Katica.
characters.voice: an old man, gravelly, slow and plain, reading a list like a ship's log

characters.name: Katica Bašić
characters.looks: From the source book "The Lighthouse That Kept Lists": Mara's grandmother, Ante's wife, died years ago. She liked lemon in her tea; Ante kept buying lemons every Monday after her death.

characters.name: Luka
characters.looks: From the source book "The Lighthouse That Kept Lists": Dino's nephew, forty-one, the island's youngest resident, mends nets and phones. Minor.

places.name: The harbour
places.looks: Outdoors. A small stone harbour on a grey Dalmatian island in November: a curved stone quay (the riva) with bollards, stone houses climbing a hill behind, café chairs stacked and chained on tables, a white car ferry at the ramp, and at the far end a long low stone causeway with an iron rail leading to a white lighthouse on a rock. Bora wind, white streaks on dark blue-grey water, sea smoke at night, warm yellow lamplight from one shop window.

places.name: Ante's house
places.looks: Indoors and doorway. A small old stone house above the harbour: a green wooden front door, a narrow kitchen with whitewashed walls, a gas ring, an oilcloth table with bin bags and a laptop, handwritten lists in capitals pinned on every wall and the fridge. Cool morning light through a small window.

places.name: Ivka's shop
places.looks: Indoors. A tiny village shop: wooden counter with an old metal till and a biscuit tin, shelves of tinned fish, bread loaves, a crate of yellow lemons, dried figs strung on a cord behind the till, batteries and rope. Warm yellow bulb light against the grey day outside the window.

places.name: Ivka's back room
places.looks: Indoors at night. A narrow warm storeroom behind the shop: shelves of tinned tomatoes to the ceiling, a crooked 2011 calendar, a ticking paraffin heater with an orange glow, a card table under the window holding a silver cassette recorder, a black ham radio with a hand microphone, a shoebox of cassettes, a cup of coffee.

places.name: The service room
places.looks: Indoors, at the foot of the lighthouse. A small round room with whitewashed curved walls and a steel door: a grey teleprinter the size of a sewing machine on a steel desk, yellowed paper rolling up out of it, a cream metal radio receiver with one big dial and two small lamps, one red and one green, an upturned wooden crate, a shelf with two jam jars. A single bare bulb; the sweep of the lighthouse beam flashes past the small window at night.

A small round room with whitewashed curved walls and a steel door: a grey teleprinter the size of a sewing machine on a steel desk, yellowed paper rolling up out of it, a cream metal radio receiver with one big dial and two small lamps, one red and one green, an upturned wooden crate, a shelf with two jam jars. A single bare bulb; the sweep of the lighthouse beam flashes past the small window at night. In frame: Mara (crying, still talking); Dino (gentle, handkerchief held out). Bora wind, white streaks on dark blue-grey water, sea smoke at night, warm yellow lamplight from one shop window. In frame: Dino (clipboard, quietly triumphant). No text, no captions, no watermark.
